level1.text: On a building site the noise level of a hammer drill at the user's ear is $91\,\text{dB}$. Using the tool without hearing protectors, in how many hours does the user receive the same energy dose as in the exposure that corresponds to the upper action value, $8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$? Answer in hours.

A ventilation unit has two identical fans. When only one is running, the noise level at the door of the machine room is $70\,\text{dB}$. What is the level at the same place when both fans are running?

The level of a loudspeaker at a garden party is $88\,\text{dB}$ at a distance of $4.0\,\text{m}$. What is the level at a distance of $8.0\,\text{m}$? Treat the loudspeaker as a point source in an open space with no reflections.
The noise level of a pneumatic hammer at the user's ear is $106\,\text{dB}$. The user wears ear defenders whose attenuation is $23\,\text{dB}$. What is the noise level reaching the ear?

To which point of noise control, the source, the path or the ear, does each measure belong? a) a noise barrier beside a motorway, b) enclosing a compressor in a sound-absorbing casing, c) earplugs, d) sound-absorbing panels in the ceiling of a factory hall.
level1.answer: a) path, b) source, c) ear, d) path

level1.text: In a school classroom speech sounds muddled because the reverberation time is too long. Which measure would shorten the reverberation time of the classroom?
level1.answer: Porous panels that absorb part of the sound hitting them are fitted in the ceiling.

choices.text: Glossy tiles are fitted on the walls, reflecting the sound evenly back into the room.
choices.feedback: Wrong: hard and smooth surfaces reflect sound almost completely, so the sound circulates in the room longer and the reverberation time gets longer.

choices.text: The person speaking is asked to talk more quietly, so the sound has time to die away faster.
choices.feedback: Wrong: the reverberation time is the time in which the level falls by $60\,\text{dB}$, and it does not depend on the initial level of the sound. It is determined by the surfaces of the room.

choices.text: Porous panels that absorb part of the sound hitting them are fitted in the ceiling.
choices.feedback: Correct: soft and porous surfaces dampen the reflected sound, so the level falls faster and the reverberation time gets shorter.

choices.text: Large glass surfaces are added to the room, letting the sound out without reflecting it back.
choices.feedback: Wrong: glass is a hard surface that reflects sound almost as well as concrete. Sound is dampened by porous, soft materials.

level1.text: Next to the outer wall of a residential building the traffic noise level is $68\,\text{dB}$. Inside, with the windows closed, the level is $41\,\text{dB}$. By how many decibels do the wall and the windows together attenuate the noise?
How does a loudspeaker produce sound from an electrical signal?
level1.answer: The alternating current in the coil and the magnet make the cone vibrate, and the cone pushes the air.

choices.text: The current of the signal heats the air behind the cone, and the expansion of the air is heard as sound.
choices.feedback: Wrong: in a loudspeaker the sound comes from the movement of the cone, not from the heating of the air. Heat is produced only as wasted energy.

choices.text: A magnet rotates steadily inside the coil, and the frequency of the rotation is the frequency of the sound.
choices.feedback: Wrong: a loudspeaker has no rotating magnet. The magnet stays in place and the frequency of the sound is determined by the variation of the current in the coil.

choices.text: The pressure variations of the sound move a diaphragm, and the movement of the diaphragm induces an alternating voltage in the coil.
choices.feedback: Wrong: this describes a microphone, in which sound moves a diaphragm and the movement is converted into a voltage. In a loudspeaker the direction is the opposite.

choices.text: The alternating current in the coil and the magnet make the cone vibrate, and the cone pushes the air.
choices.feedback: Correct: an alternating current in a magnetic field makes the coil and the cone attached to it vibrate, and the cone produces a sound wave in the air.

level1.text: The figure shows typical sound levels on a decibel scale. Read the noise level of a lawn mower from the figure. In how many hours does the mower's user, without hearing protectors, receive the same energy dose as in the exposure that corresponds to the upper action value, $8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$? Answer in hours.

level2.text: A factory hall has two identical machines. Each alone produces a level of $85\,\text{dB}$ at the worker's position. In how many hours does a worker in the hall without hearing protectors receive the daily energy dose that corresponds to the upper action value ($8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$) when both machines are running? Answer in hours.

A student listens to music with headphones on bus journeys for a total of $1.5\,\text{h}$ a day, and the level at the student's ear is about $94\,\text{dB}$. What percentage is the student's daily dose of the dose that corresponds to the upper action value ($8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$)?

The noise level of a lawn mower is $78\,\text{dB}$ at a distance of $2.0\,\text{m}$. A neighbour wants the level on their terrace to be at most $60\,\text{dB}$. How far from the mower should the terrace be? Treat the mower as a point source in an open space.

Hands are clapped once in an empty classroom. A sound level app on a phone shows that after the clap the level falls from $92\,\text{dB}$ to $62\,\text{dB}$ in $0.45\,\text{s}$. Assume the level falls steadily.

The reverberation time is the time in which the level falls by $60\,\text{dB}$, but it can be deduced even if the level cannot be followed through the whole drop of $60\,\text{dB}$.

What is the reverberation time of the classroom?

Acoustic panels were installed in the ceiling of a classroom. The sound level after a clap was measured with a phone before the panels and after the panels, at the same moments. Assume that the level falls steadily in both measurements.

The reverberation time is the time in which the level falls by $60\,\text{dB}$. Determine the reverberation time of each measurement from the first and the last row of the table.

By what percentage did the panels shorten the reverberation time?

level2.text:
A noise barrier is being planned beside a road. The level of a point source of sound was measured at the same place without the barrier and behind the barrier at different frequencies (example data).

a) By how many decibels more does the barrier attenuate sound of frequency $4000\,\text{Hz}$ than sound of frequency $500\,\text{Hz}$?

b) Explain using wavelength why a low sound is attenuated less behind the barrier. The speed of sound in air is $343\,\text{m/s}$ and the barrier is $3.0\,\text{m}$ high.

Write the result of part a) in the answer box.

data.caption: Level without the barrier and behind the barrier (example data)

level2.text:
At a workstation in a machine shop the noise level is $109\,\text{dB}$. A student calculates the daily reference time from the upper action value ($8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$) like this: “The level exceeds the action value by $24\,\text{dB}$, and every additional $3\,\text{dB}$ divides the time: $24\,\text{dB} : 3\,\text{dB} = 8$, so the reference time is $8\,\text{h} : 8 = 1.0\,\text{h}$.”

a) Explain what is wrong in the student's reasoning.

b) Calculate the correct reference time in minutes.

Write the result of part b) in the answer box.

A small compressor at a building site can be regarded as a point source. Its noise level was measured in an open field at four distances, and the readings are in the table (example data). The uncertainty of each reading is $\Delta L = 1\,\text{dB}$.

Which conclusion does the data support?
level2.answer: The level drops by about $6\,\text{dB}$ every time the distance doubles, that is, by about the same amount in every interval.

choices.text: The level roughly halves every time the distance doubles, that is, the level is inversely proportional to the distance.
choices.feedback: The decibel scale is logarithmic, and the level does not halve: half of $91\,\text{dB}$ would be about $46\,\text{dB}$, but $85\,\text{dB}$ was measured. With every doubling the level decreases by the same number of decibels.

choices.text: The level drops by about $6\,\text{dB}$ every time the distance doubles, that is, by about the same amount in every interval.
choices.feedback: Correct: the drops are $6\,\text{dB}$, $6\,\text{dB}$ and $5\,\text{dB}$. They differ from the expected $6\,\text{dB}$ by at most $1\,\text{dB}$, which is less than the uncertainty of the difference, $2\,\text{dB}$.

choices.text: In the last interval the level dropped by only $5\,\text{dB}$, so farther from the source the sound is damped more slowly.
choices.feedback: The uncertainty was ignored. The uncertainty of the difference of two readings is at most $2\Delta L = 2\,\text{dB}$, so $5\,\text{dB}$ and $6\,\text{dB}$ cannot be measurably distinguished. A single deviation does not show a new phenomenon.

choices.text: At the distance $4.0\,\text{m}$ the level does not exceed $85\,\text{dB}$, so one can work there safely for $8\,\text{h}$.
choices.feedback: Because of the uncertainty the real level can be $84$–$86\,\text{dB}$, so the upper action value may be exceeded. In addition, the upper action value is not a safety limit: staying below the reference dose does not guarantee safe hearing, and the lower action value $80\,\text{dB}$ is exceeded already.

level2.text: The figure shows typical sound levels on a decibel scale. Read the noise level of a rock concert from the figure. In how many minutes does a listener, without hearing protectors, receive the same energy dose as in the exposure that corresponds to the upper action value, $8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$? Answer in minutes.

level3.text: A warehouse worker spends $4.0\,\text{h}$ of the working day at the loading dock, where the noise level is $88\,\text{dB}$, and the remaining $4.0\,\text{h}$ in the packing room, where the level is $82\,\text{dB}$. What percentage is the worker's daily dose of the dose that corresponds to the upper action value ($8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$)?

Two terraced houses each have an identical air-source heat pump outdoor unit in the yard. The level of each unit is $55\,\text{dB}$ at a distance of $3.0\,\text{m}$. The bedroom window of a third house is $12\,\text{m}$ from each unit. What is the level at the window when both units are running? Treat the units as point sources in an open space.

Noise-cancelling headphones dampen the low hum of an aircraft engine, whose frequency is about $100\,\text{Hz}$, well. The speech of passengers, whose frequencies are about $1000$–$3000\,\text{Hz}$, can be heard through clearly better. Explain the difference using wavelengths and phase, when the speed of sound in air is $343\,\text{m/s}$.
level3.answer: The wavelength of the hum is about $3.4\,\text{m}$ and its period $10\,\text{ms}$, so the anti-noise stays in the opposite phase at the ear; the wavelength of speech is only about $11$–$34\,\text{cm}$, and even a small difference in timing or position spoils the cancellation.

level3.text:
The noise exposure of a worker in a carpenter's workshop has been measured at the worker's ear in three stages of work (example data). The worker does not wear hearing protectors. At other times the level is so low that it is not counted.

a) Calculate the day's dose as a percentage of the dose corresponding to the upper action value ($8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$).

b) By how many decibels must hearing protectors attenuate at least so that the dose does not exceed the reference dose? Assume that the attenuation is the same in all stages.

c) The employer considers enclosing the saw, which would lower the level of sawing by $10\,\text{dB}$. Is that enough alone? Justify by calculation and propose one other measure in addition.

Write the result of part b) in the answer box.

data.caption: Noise level and duration by stage of work (example data)

level3.text:
At an outdoor festival one loudspeaker stack produces a level of $112\,\text{dB}$ at a distance of $2.0\,\text{m}$. Treat the stack as a point source in an open space without reflections: the level falls by $6\,\text{dB}$ every time the distance doubles. A listener stands still at a distance of $8.0\,\text{m}$.

The listener has foam earplugs that do not fit tightly: their attenuation is in practice only $8\,\text{dB}$ at all levels.

a) What is the noise level at the listener's position without earplugs?

b) In how many hours does the listener, standing there with the earplugs, receive the energy dose that corresponds to the upper action value ($8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$)?

c) The concert lasts $3.0\,\text{h}$. What percentage of the reference dose is the dose, and does the dose stay below the reference dose if the listener moves to a distance of $16\,\text{m}$ and keeps the earplugs in there? Justify by calculation.

Write the result of part b) in the answer box.
